answer: Random memory-hard audits force each seat to keep its own key-bound working set hot. Every epoch a beacon picks 40 seats at once; each must recompute 64 random pages from a 2 GB dataset derived from its public key - the same store it used to index an atlas tile, price dried yarrow, or grade an opal cut - and answer within 3 seconds. Missing the window costs the 400 POA bond. Because the probes land together, 500 fakes need about 1 TB of RAM resident at that instant; paging from disk fails the deadline.
